resources.string: Shield, send and withdraw your own crypto privately, through Privacy Pools.
This build has no WalletConnect project ID, so it can\'t connect a wallet.

Your wallet signs one message (twice, to check it always signs the same way). The signature makes this account\'s private keys, so the same wallet can always get back into it, here or in 0xbow\'s own Privacy Pools app. Then your wallet publishes the account\'s keys once, which costs a little gas.
Up to %1$s in one send or withdrawal
Screening declined %1$s %2$s. Tap to take it back out to the address it came from.
0xbow\'s screening didn\'t approve this deposit, so it can\'t be sent privately. Exiting returns it, publicly, to the address that deposited it. Your wallet sends the transaction and pays the gas.
Waiting for the transaction to confirm…
Scan this with a wallet on your phone, or open a wallet installed here. Your wallet keeps its keys and asks you to approve everything.
Open a wallet on this phone
Waiting for your wallet to approve…
No wallet on this phone opens WalletConnect links. Scan the code with your phone instead.
Moves crypto from your wallet into the pool. 0xbow screens each deposit before it can be sent privately; that usually takes a little while. Stablecoins and ETH earn Aave yield while they\'re in.
Sends to another wallet inside the pool. Nobody can see who sent it, who got it, or how much. They see it in any Privacy Pools app with their own wallet.
Sends out of the pool to any address. A new address with no history keeps it from being linked to you. Waiting a while after shielding, and withdrawing a different amount, help too.
They receive %1$s %2$s. The relayer\'s fee, on top, is %3$s %4$s.
Shielded. It can be sent once 0xbow\'s screening approves it.

Your wallet signed the same message two different ways, so this account\'s keys couldn\'t be made again later. Use a wallet with standard signatures.

Shield is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. Its source is in the Virtroid repository, under android-client/shield. It runs 0xbow\'s Privacy Pools v2 SDK (MIT) with snarkjs and circomlib (GPL-3.0); the proving keys are from Privacy Pools\' trusted-setup ceremony.
